texts.orig: 23. NSF Indicators 2012, Figure O-2. Available at http://www.nsf.gov/statistics/seind12/pdf/overview.pdf. According to Indicators 2012, the largest global Science and Technology (S&T) gains occurred in the so-called ' Asia-10'China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan and Thailand-as those countries integrate S&T into economic growth. Between 1999 and 2009, the U.S. share of global research and development (R&D) dropped from 38 percent to 31 percent, whereas it grew from 24 percent to 35 percent in the Asia region during the same time.
